title: Joining Marion Hardy's Alabamians in Chicago
summary: Back in New York he joined Hardy's Alabamians, working out of Chicago with Sonny Boy Williams, Eddie Mallory and Charlie Turner, until a Cotton Pickers offer came.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So you sailed back to New York and what happened -- I know you joined Marion Hardy's Alabamians at that point, but was that the first thing you did?
That was the first thing because --
And you joined them in New York?
Did you join them in New York?

Yes. No, not in New York, they were at the Savoy, I went by to hear this band. Now that was a band -- there was a band who [had] -- yes, that's right, I went by the Savoy to hear this band. They had sent for me. Heard I was back.

And I went by the band to hear this band. Now there was also a band -- now I don't know whether this is the same band or not, it was headed -- that Cab was directing at that time. Now I wonder sometimes if that was

the same band, because I also heard Cab around that time and with some band, I don't know I think that was the same band, Hardy's Alabamians. They had a fellow singing with them -- when I joined them, by the name of Sonny Boy Williams. And he was imitating Cab. It could've been Sonny Boy Williams.
The original -- the old blues singer, Sonny --
Oh, no, there's another, young Sonny Boy Williams.
This guy was terrific. He was with Hardy's Alabamians when I joined them.

And so I joined Hardy, it must've been oh, let me see now. I joined Hardy's band -- I think I went to Chicago to join that band. Cause that was their headquarters. And they worked out of Chicago. Eddie Mallory was a trumpet player in the band. And Charlie Turner, bass player. That's right, I went to Chicago and joined that band. And their headquarters out of Chicago. We did one-night stands all over everywhere, Iowa and Chicago, jumping out of cars and I stayed with that band until I got an offer to go to the Cotton Pickers and that's where I wanted to be.
Now that must've been very exciting.
That was the band I wanted in the first
place, that's one reason I came back, I wanted to see if I could get with that band.
